newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end lower on bank, finance loan woes.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end lower on bank, finance loan woes.

text.p: Thai stocks closed lower in thin trade on Monday after investors unloaded bank and finance shares on concern over an approaching schedule for them to disclose their non-performing loans from July, brokers said.

"Investors are worried that non-performing loans which financial institutions will have to detail for the first time from the end of this month would rise. The jitters triggered the bank and finance sell-off today," said Padermpob Songkroh of Nava Finance and Securities.
The composite SET index fell 4.05 points to 511.55 on 2.9 billion baht turnover.
The banking sector topped the active list, falling 2.77 percent. The finance sector shed 3.08 percent.
The communications counter gained 1.82 percent, the building and construction materials stocks rallied 0.47 percent, and the energy sector rose 0.13 percent.
"I think investors switch to these sectors because they have been deeply discounted," said Padermpob.
The SET-50 index slipped 0.42 point to 36.25.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list, falling seven baht to 132, TV station operator BEC World gained 10 to 210, Finance One slipped 0.60 to 5.40, and TelecomAsia rose 1.50 to 26.75.
Brokers said they expected the index to fall slightly on Tuesday due to persistent market concern over rising non-performing loans of financial institutions.
